plan.design: Three Deployments rendered by the component. (1) The app keeps its name, labels and selector app=<h> (Service <h>, the NetworkPolicy podSelector and the consumer's server-side-apply patch all key off them) and keeps envoy-dispatch plus the cloud-sql-proxy sidecar; replicas comes from the new input, strategy is Recreate at 1 and RollingUpdate{maxUnavailable:0,maxSurge:1} above 1. (2) <h>-tailnet, 1 replica, Recreate always, the tailscale container alone, same ServiceAccount <h> and same TS_KUBE_SECRET=<h>-tailscale-state so the Role and RoleBinding the deploy account may not change stay untouched and the consumer's single-use key is never redeemed again; Serve proxies to http://<h>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local:8766 and TS_SOCKS5_SERVER binds 0.0.0.0:1055 behind a Service, since the tailscale container is also the pod's only egress to the NATS hub. (3) <h>-listener, 1 replica, Recreate always, because two listeners with one machine id never both bind. The listener binds 0.0.0.0 and so needs a bearer (validateListenerAPIAuth): a fourth RandomPassword, Secret <h>-listener, ENVOY_API_TOKEN in the listener and the same value as ENVOY_TOKEN in envoy-dispatch, ENVOY_URL at the listener Service. The app DependsOn the front-door Deployment and Service (dispatch exits 1 without NATS and /healthz is 503, so it can never go ready before the proxy exists). NetworkPolicies: <h> admits app=<h>-tailnet on 8766, <h>-tailnet admits 1055 from app=<h> and app=<h>-listener only, <h>-listener admits 9020 from app=<h> only.
plan.inputs: One new input: Replicas *int `pulumi:"replicas,optional"`, default 1, refused below 1 by name in newDispatchSettings before anything registers, with a refusal-table row and a construct row for an output-valued plain input. No strategy/maxSurge/maxUnavailable/frontDoorReplicas/listenerReplicas inputs: the safe strategy is a function of the replica count, and every value but 1 for the other two is wrong. An int carries no nkey seed, so no dispatchSeededInput row.

plan.notMyIssue: The envoy-dispatch server is not safe at two concurrent processes: the two delivery durables are exclusive push durables (one binder wins, the other logs a bind error forever), the SSE broker and live document rooms are per-process, the outbox publisher claims nothing, and several loops run once per process. The component therefore ships the capability with the default at 1 and says so in its README. A sibling issue must make the server multi-process safe before INFRA-63 sets more than one replica in production; the architect was asked to file it.

findings.finding: F1: no deliverable makes the server safe at two concurrent processes, and all three acceptance criteria are satisfiable by rendering, yet INFRA-63 is specified to set replicas above one in production.
findings.answer: The plan ships the component capability with the default at 1 (Recreate at 1 keeps today's semantics exactly), records the server's unsafety in packages/envoy/infra/README.md, lists the server work item by item in plan.md section 7, and asks the architect to file it as a sibling that blocks INFRA-63's replica change.

findings.finding: F2: a rolling update at one replica already overlaps two tailscaled processes, and a per-replica design would need a tailnet key minted in the consumer repository, which these agents cannot write.
findings.answer: The design keeps exactly one tailnet node, in its own 1-replica Deployment with the same state Secret, so the consumer's single-use key still works and no consumer change gates this issue. The one-off cutover overlap and the recommendation to mint the key reusable in future are in the handoff's apply notes.

findings.finding: F3: the Tailscale sidecar is also the pod's only egress to NATS, so moving the node out of the pod deletes it.
findings.answer: The front door exposes TS_SOCKS5_SERVER on 0.0.0.0:1055 behind a ClusterIP Service; the app and the listener take that address, a NetworkPolicy fences 1055 to those two workloads, and the app DependsOn the front-door Deployment and Service because dispatch exits 1 without NATS and /healthz is 503 until it connects. A test asserts both containers' proxy address and the policy.

findings.finding: F4: the Deployment's selector is immutable and the consumer patches that Deployment by name, so a renamed or re-kinded workload fails the preview criterion by construction.
findings.answer: The app Deployment keeps its name, namespace, labels and selector; a test asserts the selector is exactly {app: <h>} and the name <h>. The consumer's server-side-apply patch keeps targeting the same Deployment and the same envoy-dispatch container.

findings.finding: F5: rolling voids R26's recorded reason for running no pre-deploy census, and the guidance on main already claims a deployment runs one.
findings.answer: Building a census gate is not in this issue's deliverables, so the plan corrects the guidance instead (task 10 rewrites the census section's claim and names the lock-timeout consequence) and reports the gate itself to the architect as a possible separate issue.

findings.finding: F6: the rule deliverable 2 asks for is not the rule the census already enforces, and it must sit beside the census rules rather than in a new file.
findings.answer: Task 10 writes it as an expand/contract rule at the end of 'Database migrations' in packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/README.md, immediately before 'Pre-deploy census', with pointers from packages/envoy/AGENTS.md and the infra README, and states what the census does not cover (drops, renames, type changes, constraint tightening, and the one-release gap).

findings.finding: F7: deliverable 2 lands on a branch Dispatch's contributors do not read, since the component lives only on envoy-infra-integration and no issue in the family merges it to main.
findings.answer: The rule lands with the rest on the branch (one issue, one pull request, as the daemon's workflow requires), and the architect is asked to decide the follow-up that merges the branch to main or records that it never does. Recorded as a spec departure below.

findings.finding: F8: no agent can run the pulumi preview acceptance criterion, and its prerequisites are writes to a repository these agents cannot write.
findings.answer: Measured and recorded: 403 on the state bucket, no pulumi/gcloud/cluster access. The implementer opens a dispatch ask to the project owner with the exact commands and the two questions, records the full object inventory in the handoff (the criterion's own alternative clause), and proves the in-repo half with the component tests, the schema read and the selector/name assertions that are the only in-place-immutable fields. The architect is asked whether the criterion is INFRA-62's or INFRA-63's.

findings.finding: F9: 'the generated SDK is regenerated with it' has no referent inside sjawhar/legion - the only copy is the consumer's.
findings.answer: Read as the plugin's schema carrying the input, proved with pulumi package get-schema and pulumi package gen-sdk against a plugin built from this commit plus a throwaway Go build that sets Replicas. The consumer's checked-in copy is INFRA-63's stated scope; the architect is asked to confirm.

findings.finding: F10: 'the same refusals its other inputs have' is underspecified for a numeric input, and the plain-vs-Input choice and the default are open.
findings.answer: replicas is a plain *int, optional, default 1, refused below 1 by name before anything registers, with a refusal-table row and a construct test that an output-valued replicas is refused with nothing registered; no seed row, because an int cannot carry one. The default leaves every existing stack's rendering unchanged.

findings.finding: F11: 'the front door reachable throughout' and 'asserted rather than described' have no stated check.
findings.answer: Taken as rendering assertions, enumerated in plan.md section 5 - including the one that states reachability in the only form a mock engine can: rendering twice with different envoyImage and asserting the front-door Deployment's inputs are identical while the app's template differs. Live reachability is INFRA-63's 250 ms poll; the architect is asked to confirm the reading.

findings.finding: F12: the front-door redesign reaches the Role, the RoleBinding and the NetworkPolicy, the first two being objects the deploy account may not change.
findings.answer: The design touches neither Role nor RoleBinding (same ServiceAccount, same state Secret name) and says so explicitly in the handoff inventory; the NetworkPolicy work is spelled out (the app admits the front door on 8766, two new policies fence 1055 and 9020) and asserted by tests.

findings.finding: F13: three spec claims unverified and one contradicted - the container environment is not a fixed literal the consumer cannot add to, since the consumer already patches it.
findings.answer: Reported to the architect for the spec's next version (the planner does not edit the spec); the plan adds no env-var input on the strength of that sentence, and treats 'about a minute' as unmeasured, with INFRA-63's poll as the first real number.

specDepartures.spec: Deliverable 1 frames the open design choice as the Tailscale node alone: 'How the front door is arranged - the Tailscale node moved out of the pod, shared, or made per-replica - is yours to design'.
specDepartures.plan: The plan also moves envoy-listener out of the replicated pod into a 1-replica Deployment of its own with a ClusterIP Service and a generated bearer token, so the component renders three workloads rather than two.
specDepartures.evidence: Two listeners with one machine id never both bind: the second polls the exclusive durable for 135 s and exits (cmd/listener/durable.go bindListenerDurable, cmd/listener/main.go's bind), and delivery routes by machine id. A listener in its own pod must bind 0.0.0.0, which validateListenerAPIAuth refuses without ENVOY_API_TOKEN (cmd/listener/apiauth.go), hence the new Secret and RandomPassword.

outcome.scope: The component also renders Deployment <h>-listener, Service <h>-listener, NetworkPolicy <h>-listener, Secret <h>-listener and a fourth RandomPassword, and the app's ENVOY_URL and ENVOY_TOKEN change. No acceptance line changes.

specDepartures.spec: Deliverable 2: the migration rule is 'written where Dispatch's contributors read it before they write a migration', and acceptance 3: 'The migration rule exists in the repository's own guidance, not only in this issue'.
specDepartures.plan: The rule lands in packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/README.md - the file those contributors read - but on envoy-infra-integration, the branch the spec requires this work to land on. A contributor who branches from main sees it only once that branch merges to main, and no issue in this family merges it.
specDepartures.evidence: main carries no packages/envoy/infra/gcp/dispatch*.go, so the component change cannot land on main; Legion's workflow gives an issue one branch and one pull request. INFRA-63 and INFRA-64 move pins rather than merge the branch.

acceptance: Acceptance 3 is met on the issue's own branch, not on main; the architect decides the follow-up that merges envoy-infra-integration to main or records that it never does.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 2: 'pulumi preview of the consuming stack (run there, with the plugin built from your commit) shows the deployment rolling rather than being replaced'.
specDepartures.plan: No role on this issue runs it. The implementer asks the project owner to run it through a dispatch ask carrying the commit, the exact commands and the two questions it answers, records the full object inventory in the handoff under the criterion's own alternative clause, and proves the in-repo half (the component tests, the schema read, and the assertions on the only fields whose change would make the preview a replacement).
specDepartures.evidence: Measured in the worker pod: no pulumi, no gcloud, no Docker, no cluster access, and HTTP 403 on storage.objects.list for the Pulumi state bucket under the pod's Workload Identity; the consuming repository is read-only to these agents, and its deploy workflow previews only in a run a person starts on main.

acceptance: Acceptance 2's preview is proven by the project owner (or by INFRA-63's apply, whose first step is the same preview), not by this issue's implementer; the architect decides which.
